name: Street Custom 'Gallows' Recurve Bow
description:
A handmade recurve bow assembled from salvaged composite materials — typically automotive leaf springs, industrial cable for the string, and scrap polymer for the riser. The Gallows represents the lowest-tech weapon in GLMZ that remains genuinely lethal at range. With no electromagnetic components, no battery, no firmware, and no acoustic signature, it is invisible to every detection system in the city. It is a stick that throws smaller sticks, and in a world of networked surveillance, that simplicity is a superpower.

Gallows bows are built by hand in the Shelf, each one unique, each one reflecting the builder's available materials and skill level. Draw weights range from 20 to 60 kilograms depending on the spring steel used, and accuracy depends entirely on the archer's practice. The arrows are similarly improvised — metal rod shafts with filed points, stabilized with whatever passes for fletching. Despite the crude construction, a Gallows arrow through the throat kills as effectively as any precision-manufactured projectile.

The bow has become a symbol of Shelf resistance culture — a weapon that the surveillance state literally cannot see. No electronics to detect, no chemical propellant to sniff, no electromagnetic signature to track. A person with a Gallows bow and sufficient skill can kill from rooftop distance and leave no forensic trace that any automated system can process. The kill has to be investigated by humans, and there aren't enough investigators to cover the Shelf.
legality: Unregulated — not classified as a weapon under current GLMZ ordinances
specifications:
draw weight: 20-60 kg (varies by construction)
effective range: 30-60 meters (operator dependent)
arrow velocity: 50-80 m/s
weight: 1-2 kg
acoustic signature: Negligible
electronic signature: None
tactical_use: Silent elimination and harassment in environments where every other weapon would be detected. Shelf archers operate from rooftops and elevated positions, firing into streets and corridors below. The weapon's lack of any electronic signature makes it impossible to trace through automated systems — investigation requires physical evidence and human detective work.
cultural_context: The Gallows bow has become a folk icon in the Shelf. Archery practice is a community activity, and skilled archers are respected as defenders. The weapon's name references both its killing capability and the improvised gallows-frame shape of the bow when strung. 'Drawing the Gallows' is Shelf slang for taking a stand against impossible odds.
known_users: Individuals who cannot afford or access firearms
At least one vigilante known as 'the Fletcher'
story_hooks: A corporate executive was killed by an arrow — a sharpened metal rod fired from a Gallows bow — in the middle of a secured Tier 4 district. Every surveillance system in the area recorded nothing. The arrow came from somewhere that doesn't exist according to the building plans.

Someone is teaching archery classes in the Shelf, training dozens of residents in Gallows bow construction and marksmanship. The classes are free, the instructor is unknown, and the skill level of the graduates is suspiciously professional.

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal, brutalist recurve bow with pronounced curves at both limbs. The riser is a bare amalgamation of welded steel and polymer plates, held together with visible cable ties and industrial rivets. The limbs curve back sharply, almost menacing, giving it a predatory insect silhouette. There's nothing sleek about it — every element screams improvised survival engineering.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 160-180 cm. Riser width 4-6 cm, limb thickness 2-3 cm. Draw depth approximately 25 cm at full draw. Arrow shelf 8-10 cm from riser centerline.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but not unwieldy — 1.2 to 1.8 kg distributed along the limbs makes it feel alive in the hands, with tension always present. The weight bias toward the limb tips creates a sense of coiled spring potential.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered automotive leaf spring steel forming the limbs; welded steel plate and scrap polymer composite for the riser; industrial aircraft cable for the bowstring (typically 3-4mm diameter, frayed at the nocking points).
physical_description.finish: Battle-worn and oxidized. Primary limbs show varying degrees of rust patina — some areas polished by handling, others streaked with red oxide. The riser is a patchwork: bare welded seams with scale, areas of chipped black paint, bare polymer showing through worn synthetic coating. No protective lacquer — just raw material aged by exposure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal to gunmetal gray limbs with rust-orange patina streaks. Riser a chaotic mixture of black primer, bare steel silver, and tan/cream polymer. Cable bowstring appears worn hemp-brown with frayed gray fibers at the nocking loops.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rough and intentional — wrapped with water-damaged athletic tape or fabric strips, textured for purchase without slip. Some builders use bare welded steel, which is unforgiving but honest. The grip surface is never smooth; every hand that's held it has left micro-abrasions.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical limb curves reflecting the specific leaf springs salvaged
Three-point cable attachment system using crimped steel ferrules and safety wire
Arrow shelf fashioned from a single piece of beveled spring steel, sharp edges filed smooth by use
Nocking points marked with wrap-around tape or burned-in leather burns — no paint (paint flakes in the rain)
Visible stress cracks in the limb material, deliberately reinforced with backing cable to prevent failure
Crude sight reference — sometimes just a file mark on the riser, sometimes a tiny notch cut by the builder
No manufacturer nameplate — only crude scratch marks or burn marks identifying the builder (if at all)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Unmarked or bearing only the builder's street tag burned into the riser with a heating element. Some Gallows carry initials filed into the limb or welded steel plate, but not for traceability — purely for builder pride. No serial numbers. No regulatory stamps.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and deliberately maintained in that state. Minimal cleaning — rust is armor against corrosion investigation. String shows wear at nocking points, limbs display micro-cracks from stress cycling but remain structurally sound. This is a weapon that looks broken until you draw it and feel the stored energy — then it becomes brutally sophisticated.
